Per-test contention rising while wall time falls is the signature of genuinely increased parallelism, not of tests getting cheaper. Structural win, not measurement noise.

suggestedDiffReasoning: No diff proposed, on critical-path grounds rather than for lack of candidates. The weekly medians put e2e-tests at 155.5s against a perceived total of 192s, while the web and worker test shards sit at 69s and 72.8s. Those shards therefore carry ~80s of slack and run fully parallel to e2e-tests: shaving seconds off them cannot move the headline number. The one genuinely mechanical candidate found (worker/src/__tests__/redisConsumer.test.ts:116, an unconditional 'await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2000))' used to assert a job stays 'waiting' when no worker matches) would save ~1.5s on a shard with 80s of slack, at the cost of narrowing the negative-assertion window. Not worth it, and it edges toward loosening a test purely to improve a number. bufferedStreamUploader's 3.00s test was investigated and rejected as a candidate: its internal sleeps are only 10-100ms, so the 3s is real concurrency orchestration, not a fixed wait.
